differences.title: 1. PROCESSING MODEL
differences.leftDesc: Processes data as an ordered, immutable log of events.
differences.rightDesc: Processes messages by routing them to queues.

differences.title: 2. SCALABILITY
differences.leftDesc: Designed for massive throughput and horizontal scalability.
differences.rightDesc: Scales well but excels in complex routing scenarios.

differences.title: 3. DATA PERSISTENCE
differences.leftDesc: Data retained in durable logs for configurable periods.
differences.rightDesc: Messages acknowledged after processing, then removed.

differences.title: 4. CONSUMER MODEL
differences.leftDesc: Consumers pull data from partitions at their own pace.
differences.rightDesc: Broker pushes messages to consumers actively.

differences.title: 5. USE CASES
differences.leftDesc: Ideal for real-time data pipelines and stream processing.
differences.rightDesc: Great for decoupling microservices and background jobs.

differences.title: 6. MESSAGE ORDER
differences.leftDesc: Guarantees order within a partition, not globally.

differences.title: 7. COMPLEXITY
differences.leftDesc: More complex to set up and manage, especially distributed.
differences.rightDesc: Generally easier to set up and manage for basic use.
